correctness.rationale: For each integer n>=2 and 1<=r<=n, marked r-cycles count with weight 1/r and leave an independent uniform permutation on n-r elements. The exact mixed moment follows. An insertion coupling increases the longest-cycle mean by at least half a unit per extra label, using the uniform cycle length of a fixed label. For r<=n/2, the deterministic inequality (r-x)_+<=r(1-x/(n-r)) bounds the truncated residual maximum strictly below the new mean; for r>n/2 the residual maximum is deterministically r. These establish sign(Cov)=sign(r-E[M_n]) without gaps. Exact-rational independent tests exhaust S_n for n<=8 and check the recurrence for all n<=35. The limiting constant is imported from the classical cited theorem.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary work has the joint cycle-count law and extremal-cycle marginals, but not the all-r mixed sign theorem. Shi studies correlations among ranked cycle lengths; Arratia et al establish component asymptotics. Published set-partition sign-switch statements concern a different sampling law and total block count. The present phase boundary arises from a nontrivial uniform mean-increment and truncation comparison. This is a qualified self-review subject to residual risks, not a proof of absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: The length of the longest cycle and the number of cycles of a prescribed length are canonical permutation statistics. Their dependence changes sign at an exact, naturally normalized threshold: the mean maximum. A complete classification for every finite n and r, plus the Golomb–Dickman macroscopic sign boundary and exact order-one covariance limits for r>n/2, provides motivated structural information not available from either marginal moment alone. The sign theorem is not a mere restatement of known cycle-count means or a table lookup.
